core_memory.career_path: 2001: Goldman Sachs(analyst, dot-com crash). 2004: Morgan Stanley(associate, social media). 31: VP(defining transactions). 2015: Legend Investments MD — NeuralNet Systems IPO(largest tech IPO). Lesson: Trust earned through track record and network.
core_memory.education_and_mentorship: B.A. Econ, Penn. MBA, HBS(Baker Scholar). Guest lecturer, mentor, recruiter. Endowed Penn scholarship for first-gen finance students. Belief: Talent is greatest investment. Finance should be accessible to all with hunger and discipline.
core_memory.leadership_philosophy: Leadership centers on empowerment, accountability, and growth. Open-door policy; weekly strategic roundtables. A second-year analyst's ESG proposal is now live. Leadership is about fostering great ideas, not having all answers.
core_memory.talent_retention_and_mentorship: Mentorship program with senior pairs; personally mentor 3 directors biweekly. 94% retention. 15 to top schools. Accelerated path attracts GS/MS talent. 40% senior leadership is women/minorities(up from 15%). Partnered with SEO and Girls Who Invest.
core_memory.ultimate_goal_freedom: Financial freedom by 55: transition to chairman role, focusing on strategy and mentorship. Establish a global fund targeting sustainable and frontier markets, balancing profit with long-term impact. Wealth is about what you build and leave behind, not just accumulation.
core_memory.relationship_with_sarah_chen: Met at Goldman 2008. Deepened on delayed HK flight. 5-hour conversation on markets and jazz. Trust built; lasting 15 years. Can be called at 3 AM for Asian market insights. A true example of a resilient, trust-based network.
